title: The load that counted itself done
blurb: Completion was marked before partitions committed and merges doubled.
prompt: A finance table was missing two partitions while the load reported complete, and a retried merge doubled a day of orders. The model-generated draft marks complete at read time and appends on retry. Review it, fix it, and prove completion follows partitions and retries are idempotent.
aiNote: The draft flips the completion flag when the source file is read rather than when the final partition commits, so readers can consume a load that is missing data, and its merge retry re-runs an append, duplicating rows on every timeout.
testIdea: Crash after reading the manifest and assert the load is not visible as complete; force a merge timeout and assert one row set after the retry; compare reported written counts against the warehouse.
followUps: How do you reconcile a load without re-reading the source?
What partition size keeps retries cheap?
When is merge safer than replace, and vice versa?
